claims.text: Equiatomic as-cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic as-cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance at high temperatures.
A low-temperature ALD process can apply an ultrathin, conformal alumina coating to as-cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The ALD treatment will produce a dense, adherent alumina scale on the alloy surface.
The alumina coating will act as a barrier to oxygen diffusion into the bulk alloy.
The alumina coating will form a stable, slow-growing protective oxide scale at approximately 1000 °C in an oxygen-bearing atmosphere.
The protective coating will minimize internal oxidation during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The surface treatment will preserve the original cast microstructure.
The original cast microstructure is responsible for the alloy’s favorable mechanical properties.
ALD alumina coating will substantially improve the oxidation resistance of HfNbTaTiZr relative to the untreated cast alloy.
The coated alloy will exhibit reduced oxygen penetration during prolonged exposure at approximately 1000 °C in air.
The coated alloy will exhibit reduced oxide-scale formation during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The coating will preserve room-temperature tensile ductility in the range of 8–16%.
The coating will preserve high-temperature yield strength in the range of approximately 163–530 MPa.
The coating is expected to remain effective around 1000 °C in air under mechanical loading at strain rates of 10^-4 to 10^-2 s^-1.
Long-term thermal or mechanical cycling may cause coating spallation or degradation.
